newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU to hold special meeting on future in Rome.
newsitem.headline: EU to hold special meeting on future in Rome.

text.p: Italy is to host a special meeting of European Union foreign ministers in Rome on March 25 to commemorate the 40th anniversary of one of the bloc's founding documents, the Dutch EU presidency said on Friday.

Marking the signing in 1957 of the Treaty of Rome, the meeting will also double as an opportunity for the EU ministers to discuss negotiations on the bloc's latest treaty, due to be agreed at a summit in Amsterdam in June.

The Treaty of Rome created the European Economic Community (EEC) -- comprising Italy, France, Germany, Belgium, Luxembourg and the Netherlands -- out of existing institutions linking coal, steel and atomic energy policies.
The EEC later became the European Community and, with the coming into effect of the Maastricht Treaty in 1993, the European Union.

Now comprising 15 countries and planning a huge expansion into eastern Europe, the EU is arguing that the institutions and systems it set up for six countries 40 or more years ago are no longer adequate.

Although the bloc is publicly committed to completing its new treaty by the Amsterdam summit in order to begin enlargement, Dutch and other EU officials privately admit that agreement is likely to be delayed by the British election.
Britain's Conservative government, which is opposed to many of the proposals supported by other EU countries in the negotiations, must hold an election by May at the latest.
It is widely expected to lose and many EU countries are hoping to be able to achieve more in the talks with an incoming Labour government.
There could, however, be as little as six weeks between a new government taking over and the Amsterdam summit.
This has led to the view that final decisions on the treaty will have to be put off until some time in the Luxembourg EU presidency which begins on July 1.
